rationale: Correct Duquesne Light Company's ownership ledger to the current three-vehicle structure disclosed by the company in August 2026 and in its 2025 Corporate Responsibility Report. DQE Holdings' equity is held through Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. (GIC, 44.4%), Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC (Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM, 30.4%), and AIA Montana LLC (owned by APG Americas Infrastructure and CalSTRS and managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, 25.2%). The company does not identify Macquarie as a current investor, and a New York City Comptroller infrastructure-market report records Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets' 2016 sale of its 30.4% interest to PGGM and John Hancock. Retire the Macquarie ownership period in 2016, preserve both the APG economic-owner and Argo manager relationships without treating the shared 25.2% vehicle interest as two separate economic stakes, and clarify that Manulife's record represents the shared Three Rivers vehicle. Also correct the website, Pittsburgh headquarters, current operating description, verification date, and supporting milestone evidence. Current-company and current-report exit searches found no later sale or pending ownership transaction involving the three disclosed vehicles.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Duquesne Light Company is the regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving more than 600,000 customers across Allegheny and Beaver counties, including Pittsburgh, over an approximately 812-square-mile service territory. The company does not generate power and maintains approximately 8,400 miles of transmission and distribution lines. Its parent, DQE Holdings LLC, discloses three current ownership vehicles: GIC affiliate Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. at 44.4%, Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM vehicle Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC at 30.4%, and APG/CalSTRS vehicle AIA Montana LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, at 25.2%. Macquarie's former infrastructure ownership was realized in 2016.

Duquesne Light Holdings completed its take-private by a Macquarie-led infrastructure consortium in May 2007.
Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd., a GIC affiliate, acquired DUET's interests in DQE Holdings; Duquesne reports GIC as an owner since 2011 and its current stake as 44.4%.
Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets sold its 30.4% DQE Holdings interest to PGGM and John Hancock through Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC.
AIA Montana LLC, owned by APG Americas Infrastructure and CalSTRS and managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, became a DQE Holdings owner; its current vehicle interest is 25.2%.
